open_points.subject: A18 rule 3 and rule 4 orphan value-byte lifecycle
open_points.text: Rule 3 says "value bytes are reused by equal bytes until the next start removes them", while rule 4 removes only "value bytes no record names". A successful call before restart can reuse the bytes and create a record naming them.
open_points.question: When previously orphaned value bytes are reused by a successful call and become named before the next start, does startup preserve them or remove them?
options: Preserve them because a record now names them
Remove them because rule 3 says the next start removes them
open_points.default_guess: Preserve them because the startup removal condition in rule 4 is that no record names the bytes.

open_points.subject: A18 rule 4 startup removal failure
open_points.text: "On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... are removed" specifies no outcome when an unreferenced value-byte file cannot be removed; only failure to remove an obsolete spool directory is explicitly made non-fatal.
open_points.question: What happens when startup cannot remove unreferenced value bytes: does startup fail, continue while leaving them unreadable for a later cleanup, or take another action?
options: Continue, never serve them, and retry removal at a later start
Continue without a specified retry guarantee
open_points.default_guess: Continue, never serve them, and retry removal at a later start, matching the explicit treatment of obsolete spool directories.
